name: Phenomenal Lavender Hydrosol
description: Steam-distilled from 'Phenomenal' lavender flower spikes. Sweet and floral — linalool and linalyl acetate forward, with a touch more camphor than true lavender.
description_full: Steam-distilled from our own 'Phenomenal' lavandin flower spikes, this hydrosol carries the classic floral-herbaceous bouquet of lavender — linalool and linalyl acetate forward — with a touch more camphor than true English lavender. 'Phenomenal' is a robust lavandin cultivar prized by growers for its vigor, disease resistance, and unusually high oil content, traits that carry through into a hydrosol with real depth and staying power. A go-to calming facial and body mist, a natural addition to linen and pillow sprays, or a water substitute in lotions, creams, and bath products. Also a favorite for cooling sunburned or irritated skin.
technical_note: Distilled from fresh 'Phenomenal' lavender flower spikes via steam distillation. As a lavandin (a natural hybrid of true lavender and spike lavender), its aromatic profile carries a touch more camphor than Lavandula angustifolia hydrosols, alongside the expected linalool and linalyl acetate. As with all hydrosols, natural batch variation in scent and color should be expected. Intended for cosmetic and household use only.

name: Meyer Lemon Hydrosol
description: Steam-distilled from Meyer lemon peel. A soft citrus nose — rounder and more floral than true lemon.
photo_alt: Ripe Meyer lemon hanging on the branch
description_full: Steam-distilled from Meyer lemon peel, this hydrosol trades true lemon's sharp citral edge for something softer and more floral, a natural result of Meyer lemon's lower acidity and gentler aromatic profile. A gentle, refreshing toner for all skin types, especially oily or combination skin. Mist onto the face after cleansing, use as a water substitute in lotions and creams, or add to a clay mask for a bright citrus lift. Also lovely as a light room or linen spray. Blends well with lavender, rosemary, or a few drops of Meyer lemon essential oil for a deeper citrus note.
technical_note: Distilled from fresh, rinsed Meyer lemon peel via steam distillation. As with all hydrosols, natural batch variation in scent and color should be expected. Intended for cosmetic and household use only.
sizes: 4 oz. amber glass spray / 8 oz. refill
scent: Soft citrus, rounder and more floral than true lemon
key_aromatics: Limonene-led, with less citral than true lemon
uses: Water swap in lotions and creams

name: Spearmint Hydrosol
description: Steam-distilled from spearmint leaf. Sweet and cooling — carvone forward, softer than peppermint's menthol edge.
description_full: Steam-distilled from spearmint leaf, this hydrosol carries the sweet, familiar bouquet of spearmint, built on carvone with limonene and 1,8-cineole in support. Spearmint holds little menthol, so it reads softer and sweeter than peppermint, without the sharp cooling edge. Makes a soothing facial mist for warm days or after sun exposure, a cooling toner, a water substitute in lotions and after-sun gels, or a light room and pillow spray. Pairs well with our lavender, lemongrass, or Meyer lemon hydrosols.
technical_note: Distilled from fresh spearmint leaf and stem via steam distillation. As with all hydrosols, natural batch variation in scent and color should be expected. Intended for cosmetic and household use only.

name: Rosemary Hydrosol
description: Steam-distilled from rosemary leaf. Woody and resinous — 1,8-cineole and camphor forward, with a bright pine-like lift.
photo_alt: Rosemary stems with needle-like leaves and blue flowers
description_full: Steam-distilled from rosemary leaf, this hydrosol carries a woody, resinous bouquet built on 1,8-cineole and camphor, with a bright, pine-like top note from alpha-pinene. Trailing rosemary tends to run a touch milder and less camphorous than upright culinary rosemary, giving a rounder, more wearable version of that classic evergreen scent. A brisk, invigorating facial and scalp mist, a natural water substitute in lotions and hair rinses, or a bracing addition to a morning routine. Popular in DIY hair care for the scalp, and a clean, herbaceous note in room and linen sprays.
technical_note: Distilled from fresh rosemary leaf and stem via steam distillation. As with all hydrosols, natural batch variation in scent and color should be expected. Intended for cosmetic and household use only.

name: Valencia Orange Hydrosol
description: Steam-distilled from Valencia orange peel. A bright citrus-peel nose, d-limonene forward, with a soft floral finish.
photo_alt: A pile of ripe Valencia oranges
description_full: Steam-distilled from Valencia orange peel, this hydrosol carries a true peel-oil bouquet: d-limonene up front, the same aromatic terpene that defines orange essential oil, rounding out into a soft floral finish. Gentler than the essential oil itself, it's well suited to all skin types — especially normal-to-dry skin seeking a light, non-drying toner. Use as a refreshing facial mist, a water substitute in lotions, creams, and clay masks, or as a natural room and linen spray. A cheerful addition to DIY household cleaners, where citrus's natural degreasing properties shine. Pairs well with vanilla, ginger, cinnamon leaf, or ylang ylang for a warmer, richer variation.
technical_note: Distilled from fresh-cut Valencia orange peel at low heat via steam distillation. As with all hydrosols, natural batch variation in scent and color should be expected. Intended for cosmetic and household use only.

distilled_from: Fresh-cut Valencia orange peel, distilled at low heat

name: Oregano Hydrosol
description: Steam-distilled from oregano leaf. Warm and herbaceous — carvacrol and thymol forward, edging toward medicinal.
photo_alt: Oregano flower clusters with small oval leaves
description_full: Steam-distilled from oregano leaf, this hydrosol carries oregano's signature phenolic bouquet: carvacrol and thymol forward, warm, savory, and edging toward medicinal. Naturally antimicrobial and antifungal in character, it's prized as a purifying mist for the skin and scalp, a natural addition to DIY surface cleaners, and a traditional gargle or steam-inhalation herb for seasonal wellness. Its aromatic compounds carry real bite even in hydrosol form — more so than most hydrosols — so a patch test is recommended before facial use, especially for sensitive skin.
technical_note: Distilled from fresh oregano leaf and flower via steam distillation. Naturally rich in carvacrol and other phenolic compounds. As with all hydrosols, natural batch variation in scent and strength should be expected. Intended for cosmetic and household use only; not a substitute for medical treatment.

scent: Warm, savory and herbaceous, edging toward medicinal

name: Lemongrass Hydrosol
description: Steam-distilled from lemongrass leaf and stalk. Bright and grassy — citral forward, the same top note found in lemon peel.
photo_alt: Lemongrass stalks rising into long green leaf blades
description_full: Steam-distilled from lemongrass leaf and stalk, this hydrosol carries a bright, grassy bouquet built on citral — the same aromatic aldehyde that gives lemon peel its sharp citrus top note. Lemongrass hydrosol makes a toning facial mist well suited to oily or blemish-prone skin, a refreshing addition to hair rinses, and a natural water substitute in lotions and clay masks. Popular as a base for body and room sprays, particularly blended with a few drops of citronella, lemongrass, or eucalyptus essential oil for an outdoor/insect-deterring variation. Also a bright note in DIY household cleaners.
technical_note: Distilled from fresh lemongrass stalk and leaf via steam distillation. As with all hydrosols, natural batch variation in scent and color should be expected. Intended for cosmetic and household use only.

name: White Sage Hydrosol
description: Earthy, herbaceous white sage, steam-distilled fresh. Grounding and clarifying.
photo_alt: Silvery-white leaves of California white sage
description_full: A soft, herbal, resinous water distilled from white sage — gentler and more wearable than burning the dried leaf, with the same grounding, clarifying character. Use as a room and linen spray, a calming body mist, or a light facial toner for normal-to-oily skin. White sage has long held deep cultural and ceremonial significance for Indigenous peoples of California, and wild populations have faced real pressure from over-harvesting. This hydrosol is distilled entirely from garden-grown, responsibly cultivated California white sage — never wild-harvested — so you can use it with a clear conscience.
technical_note: Distilled from fresh, garden-grown white sage leaf via steam distillation. As with all hydrosols, natural batch variation in scent and color should be expected. Intended for cosmetic and household use only.

distilled_from: Garden-grown white sage leaf, never wild-harvested

name: African Blue Basil Hydrosol
description: Steam-distilled from African blue basil leaf and flower. Camphorous and spicy — camphor and eugenol forward, with a clove-like edge.
photo_alt: African blue basil in full bloom, covered in lavender-purple flower spikes
description_full: Steam-distilled from African blue basil leaf and flower, this hydrosol carries a bold, layered bouquet: camphor and 1,8-cineole up front, a spicy eugenol edge reminiscent of clove, and a faint sweet, floral finish. African blue basil is a striking, sterile hybrid between camphor basil and dark opal basil, prized by growers for its purple-veined leaves, lavender flower spikes, and unusually rich fragrance. Bolder and more medicinal than a culinary basil hydrosol, it makes an invigorating room and body spray, a bracing addition to a post-workout mist, or a distinctive note in DIY cleaning sprays. Best appreciated by those who like their herbal scents assertive rather than delicate.
technical_note: Distilled from fresh African blue basil leaf and flower via steam distillation. As a hybrid of camphor basil (Ocimum kilimandscharicum) and basil (Ocimum basilicum), its aromatic profile is naturally higher in camphor and 1,8-cineole than culinary basil varieties. As with all hydrosols, natural batch variation in scent and color should be expected. Intended for cosmetic and household use only; the camphorous character means a patch test is recommended before facial use.
sizes: 4 oz. amber glass spray / 8 oz. refill
scent: Bold and spicy, with a clove-like edge and a faint sweet finish
distilled_from: Fresh African blue basil leaf and flower
key_aromatics: Camphor and 1,8-cineole up front, a eugenol edge
